name: iTerm2
summary: macOS-only terminal with profiles, Dynamic Profiles (JSON), color presets, background images, blur, hotkey window, shell integration and inline images.
configFormat: plist preferences; Dynamic Profiles as JSON/plist files

install.notes: Direct download from https://iterm2.com/downloads.html also works. Latest stable 3.7.9 needs macOS 13+.

macos.notes: Agents should write a Dynamic Profile JSON file into DynamicProfiles/ (loaded live; no restart); do not edit the binary preferences plist while iTerm2 runs. A malformed file in that folder makes iTerm2 skip all Dynamic Profile changes, so lint first. `plutil -lint` accepting JSON input is assumed, not confirmed in the docs read; if it rejects the file use `python3 -m json.tool {file}`. Errors are logged in Console.app. Preference-level (non-profile) settings such as tab bar position are not Dynamic Profile keys.

ligatures.notes: Enabling ligatures disables the GPU renderer.

font-fallback.notes: Profiles > Text has a Non-ASCII font and Special Exceptions (range remap, with an Install Nerd Font Bundle option). Exact Dynamic Profile key names for these were not confirmed; configure once in the UI and export the profile as JSON to read them. Simplest path: use a Nerd Font as Normal Font.

background-animated.notes: Only a static image (or a rotating folder of images) is documented for backgrounds. Use another terminal (Ghostty, kitty) for shader-driven animation.

shader.notes: No custom shader support. Use Ghostty or kitty for shaders.

padding.notes: No padding setting in the Window profile docs. iTerm2 has Advanced settings for side and top/bottom margins (TerminalMargin, TerminalVMargin via `defaults write com.googlecode.iterm2`); names unverified here, check Settings > Advanced and search 'margin'.

tabs.notes: Tab bar position and visibility are global preferences (Settings > Appearance > Tabs), not profile keys, so Dynamic Profiles cannot set them. A per-profile tab color exists (Colors tab) as `tab_color` in the Python API.

titlebar.notes: Window style (normal, no title bar, full screen, ...) is the Style option in Settings > Profiles > Window; the Dynamic Profile key is `Window Type` (enum-backed number, values not confirmed). Export a profile to read the value for the style you want.

quake.notes: Hotkey window is created through the UI; Dynamic Profile keys for hotkeys were not confirmed.

keybindings.notes: Key mappings live in Settings > Keys (global) and Profiles > Keys (per profile, stored in the profile as a key map). The serialized format was not verified; set once in the UI and export the profile JSON, or use the Python API.

startup-layout.notes: Window arrangements (Window > Save Window Arrangement; restore at launch via Settings > General > Startup) and the Python/AppleScript APIs. Not expressible as a plain config file; format not verified.
